newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada-Chicago gas pipe not ready for green light.
newsitem.headline: Canada-Chicago gas pipe not ready for green light.

text.p: A group of Canadian energy companies aiming to build a C$3.6-billion natural gas pipeline to Chicago from northern Canada is not yet ready to give a green light to the project, an official with the consortium said on Wednesday.
Alliance Pipeline must still study several special conditions put forward by potential customers during the project's call for gas commitments last month, said company vice-president Jack Crawford.

The board of Alliance met on Tuesday to consider the results of its open season, which ended November 8, and decide whether to give the project the go-ahead. The pipeline would ship 1.25 billion cubic feet per day of gas starting in 1999.
Crawford said it was unclear when a decision would be made.
"When we've got enough conditions lifted, we'll go back to the board and tell them we do. But until we do, we don't," Crawford said. "I think we've got the tools to do that but we've got work to do."

The producer-backed pipeline, which would provide competition to traditional pipeline companies such as NOVA Corp and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, would extend about 3,000 km to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia.
Its partners include such companies as Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and IPL Energy Inc.
Crawford said Alliance was proceeding with preparations for regulatory filings, despite the current uncertainty over natural gas shipping commitments.

The consortium's plans envision filing an application with the United States Federal Energy Regulatory Commission before the end of this year and another with Canada's National Energy Board by mid-1997. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
